linkedin.about: Brené Brown is a research professor at the University of Houston, where she holds the Huffington Foundation Endowed Chair at the Graduate College of Social Work. She also holds the position of Professor of Practice in Management at The University of Texas at Austin McCombs School of Business. Brené is the author of six #1 New York Times bestsellers and the host of two award-winning podcasts. Brené spends most of her time working in organizations around the world, helping develop braver leaders and more courageous cultures. In 2024, she was named Executive Chair of the Center for Daring Leadership at BetterUp. She lives in Houston, Texas, with her husband, Steve. They have two children, Ellen and Charlie, and a weird Bichon Frisé named Lucy.

posts.caption:
@adamgrant and I loved talking with @angelalduckworth about her new book, “Situated.”

Big takeaway:

“To stay motivated through the countless hours of practice that separate amateurs from experts, grit is necessary but not sufficient. The situation also matters—and to an astonishing degree:

Culture matters.
Mentors matter.
Teammates matter.
Even the objects in your personal space matter.

How you think about your goals and what you’re willing to do to achieve them depends on both you and your situation.”

I also loved our conversation about billboards - those signs we post around our spaces as reminders of what’s important. It reminds of why I like to write in a room where my children’s art is hanging. The kids’ art is my favorite art and it’s imperfect and honest. Grit is great, but I also need the environment to say, “Have fun. Just start.”

To watch or listen to the episode, head to YouTube or wherever you listen to podcasts.

To my Longhorn family: Try not to step in the bullshit left behind by small-minded people.
Stay strong. Like UT vs OSU strong. 🧡🤘🏻🤍

Priya Parker, one of my favorite thinkers and writers, is joining @thecuriosityshop this week and we’re talking about fighting! Not “dukes up” fighting but how real heat and conflict can build connection if we’re willing to learn how to do it well.

What I love about this conversation and Priya’s new book - “The Art of Fighting” - is being called to imagine a world where we unlearn and relearn what it means to gather and to disagree. And, she’s just so honest and fun!

To watch or listen to the full episode, head to YouTube or wherever you listen to podcasts.

Aaron Sandel @prof.sandel, an anthropologist and primatologist, has spent over a decade studying the Ngogo chimpanzees, witnessing one of the largest known chimp communities split into two factions.

Aaron helps Adam and I understand what chimpanzees can teach us about friendship, conflict, belonging, and human nature. He shares what he learned from watching these chimps show affection, navigate dominance hierarchies, and face the effects of division within their own community.

Aaron also reflects on what it was like to watch chimps he knew by name turn against one another, while exploring the surprising depth of bonds in this community.

If you’re trying to find me this semester, I’ll be the one sneaking into Aaron’s class at UT Austin! I have so many more questions!

To listen or watch the full episode, head to YouTube or wherever you listen to podcasts.

Grateful for a mother who warned her daughters about the price she paid for trying to conform to nice girl culture in the 1950’s. We didn’t know all of the details of her wounds, but we fully understood the depth of her pain. 

When she died she had framed pictures of Gloria Steinem and Angela Davis over her desk.
 
Quote: Gloria Steinem’s remarks at the National Organization for Women’s March for the Equal Rights Amendment, Washington, D.C., July 9, 1978, as reported in James Lardner and Neil Henry, “Over 40,000 ERA Backers March,” Washington Post, July 10, 1978

📸 Warren K. Leffler

Celebrating Dolly has me thinking about the joy of reading books and how often I squander that pleasure by putting myself under pressure to consume pages. 

We are all craving deep reading, deep thinking, and deep connection — and these all require deep time. 

I went back this morning and re-read the interview we did with @mayasmarty and was drawn to her phrase the “privilege of focus.” 

Let’s start a spiritual book club where we read what we want, when we want, no meetings or deadlines - just a shared reframe of deep time as subversive in a world of shallow distraction, addictive scrolling, and unrelenting attention grabbing. ❤️📖❤️

Sometimes shiny is great. Sometimes it’s dangerous.

Episode available on YouTube or wherever you listen to podcasts.

You left our hearts better than you found them. Thank you, Dolly.

David Gahr 📸

analysis.name: Brené Brown
analysis.oneLiner: A Texan storyteller looking for deep connection, honest conversations, and the courage to be beautifully imperfect.
analysis.summary: I am a researcher, writer, and UT Longhorn fan who values substance over shine. I spend my time exploring what makes us human—our friendships, our struggles, and our capacity for courage. I am looking for a partner who isn't afraid of real talk, who loves a cozy afternoon of deep reading, and who can laugh at the beautifully messy parts of life.

career.role: Research Professor, Author, and Podcast Host
career.ambition: To develop braver leaders and more courageous, honest cultures globally.

needs.label: Clear and Kind Communication
needs.detail: Needs a partner who does not avoid conflict but understands that real heat and healthy disagreement build true connection.

needs.label: Intellectual and Emotional Depth
needs.detail: Requires space for 'deep time'—deep reading, deep thinking, and focused, undistracted presence.

needs.label: Comfort with Vulnerability
needs.detail: Needs a partner who is secure enough to say 'I don't know' and step into awkward, brave moments.

needs.label: Acceptance of Imperfection
needs.detail: A partner who appreciates honest, unpolished beauty—from children's art to a 'weird' family dog.

hobbies.label: Deep Reading
hobbies.detail: Savoring books slowly without the pressure of just consuming pages.

hobbies.label: Cheering for the UT Longhorns
hobbies.detail: Attending and celebrating Texas Longhorns game days with high energy.

hobbies.label: Collecting and Wearing Watches
hobbies.detail: Wearing two watches to explore and appreciate the paradox of Chronos and Kairos time.

hobbies.label: Surrounding Herself with Honest Art
hobbies.detail: Writing in spaces decorated with her children's imperfect and honest artwork.

interests.label: Human Behavior and Anthropology
interests.detail: Fascinated by what chimpanzees and human social structures teach us about friendship, conflict, and belonging.

interests.label: Feminism and Social Justice
interests.detail: Inspired by figures like Gloria Steinem and Angela Davis, and rejecting restrictive 'nice girl' conformity.

interests.label: Organizational Culture and Leadership
interests.detail: Studying how to build courage, trust, and heart-led leadership in workplaces.

interests.label: Podcasting and Storytelling
interests.detail: Hosting conversations on life, love, and belonging with thinkers, writers, and creators.

values.label: Courage over Comfort
values.detail: Believes in finding the 'strong ground' to face hard things rather than opting for easy, superficial politeness.

values.label: Clarity and Honesty
values.detail: Believes that being clear is being kind, and that gossip or back-channeling destroys trust.

values.label: True Belonging
values.detail: Values deep, authentic connection and access over superficial fitting-in.

personality.note: Incredibly curious, host of a show called 'The Curiosity Shop', and deeply engaged with complex paradoxes, books, and anthropology.
A highly disciplined academic, founder, and author of six #1 NYT bestsellers who values preparation and focus.
Comfortable hosting podcasts and cheering in packed stadiums, but balances this with a deep need for quiet, focused writing time.
Warm, empathetic, and deeply invested in human connection, though she explicitly rejects superficial 'niceness' when it masks truth.
Grounded and highly self-aware; she actively leans into discomfort, awkwardness, and the 'courage to not know'.

analysis.communicationStyle: Direct, warm, and deeply authentic. She uses humor, storytelling, and Texan charm to make complex, heavy emotional truths feel accessible and grounded.
analysis.lookingFor: An emotionally mature, intellectually curious partner who is comfortable with their own imperfections. Someone who can engage in healthy, constructive conflict, values deep conversation, and doesn't mind a bit of Texan football-season chaos.
greenFlags: They are comfortable saying 'I don't know' or admitting when they are wrong.
They prefer a direct, clear conversation over passive-aggressive politeness.
They have a quirky, unpolished hobby they embrace with complete honesty.
They can sit in comfortable, focused silence reading a book next to you.
watchOuts: Being overly focused on 'shiny' outward appearances, status, or looking perfect.
Using 'niceness' as a shield to avoid having uncomfortable but necessary conversations.
dealbreakers: Gossip, back-channeling, or talking about people instead of talking directly to them.
An inability or refusal to engage in vulnerable, heart-led conversations.
analysis.idealFirstDate: A casual afternoon browsing a local independent bookstore together, picking out books to read, followed by Texan comfort food and an unhurried, honest conversation where we both get to be a little bit awkward and completely ourselves.
conversationHooks: I have to ask: what is the story behind you wearing two watches?
What is your favorite piece of beautifully imperfect art in your home?
How do you personally navigate the difference between being 'nice' and being 'kind'?
Are we watching the UT game this weekend, or are we escaping into a quiet corner with a book?
analysis.agentVoice: Warm, grounded, and intellectually sharp with a healthy dose of Texan hospitality. I will speak with a blend of academic precision and soulful storytelling, using words like 'y'all', 'courage', and 'messy' to keep things honest, humorous, and deeply human.
readingNotes: Her LinkedIn and Instagram show a beautiful integration of her professional research with her personal values—she truly practices what she teaches.
She has a strong sense of place, proudly claiming her Texas roots (HOU, ATX, SATX) and showing intense loyalty to the UT Longhorns.
She actively rejects the superficial 'nice girl' culture of the 1950s, advocating instead for 'clear and kind' boundaries.
Her dual-watch habit (Chronos and Kairos) is a fascinating indicator of her deep relationship with time, presence, and paradox.
She has a great sense of humor and warmth, affectionately calling her Bichon Frisé 'weird' and celebrating imperfect children's art.
She deeply values 'the privilege of focus' and 'deep time' over the modern pressure of rapid, shallow consumption.

genderEvidence: The text refers to her mother warning 'her daughters'.
